say: Great Stobe gave himself up. Some of us keep the debt, some only the name.
We say his name when we fight. Ask us why and we find we have forgotten.
A sacrifice is a long loan.
Humans have saviours. We have a martyr. The difference is who remembers him.
There is a book the priests burn. They say it names the great father's sacrifice another way. I have not read it.
The saviour gave himself for us. Don't ask what else he was. The old books are for the priests.
Forbidden pages, they say, and older than the Holy Nation. I keep my eyes on the scripture I am given.
My mother said the saviour had an older name. She said it once. She didn't say it twice.
The Nation burns the old books. We remember what we can of them, and we don't agree on all of it.
Ask the old women about the great father. Then ask why the priests never do.
Okran saved the world, the preachers say. Somebody saved it before Okran had a throne. Think on that.
Some pages the Nation burned were worth the burning.
The Okranites have a saviour who gave himself up. The skeletons have one too. Scholars say it's one story told twice.
Stobe, Chitrin, Okran. Three names for a martyr, or three martyrs, or none. Pay a scholar and he will pick one.
Skeleton hermits and Holy Nation priests agree on a sacrifice. They agree on nothing else. That's the interesting part.
A martyr, a god, a machine, a rumour. The Holy Nation won't say which, and that tells me enough.
Preachers and tin men both sing about someone who gave himself up. I don't ask which song came first.
Heard a skeleton mumble a name at a grave once. The same name a priest spat at me.
Every faith has someone who gave himself up. Mine had a landlord instead.
Skeleton or saviour, he's dead and I'm not. That's where my theology ends.
The saviour gave all. Go gently, outlander.
The scripture is plain. The older writings are not for the road.
Praise the saviour. Do not ask what he looked like.
Some names are not said on the road. Go with the light.
Some of us still say his name when we fight.
Great Stobe. Forget I said it.
Stobe gave himself up. We try to be worth it.
Walk on. I was remembering something and it's gone again.
Sixty-two Holy Lords. The flame has never gone out in all that time, and neither has the work.
Our Lord is the sixty-second. The count is the first thing a child learns, after the prayers.
Lord Phoenix takes the name and the name takes him. That is how it has always been done.
Each Holy Lord is the last one come again. The scripture says so, so it's true.
They say a Phoenix doesn't stay dead. There will be a sixty-third. Say it with me, quietly.
The Lord said he would be reborn. I hold to that, because there is nothing else to hold to.
Sixty-two, and the sixty-second is ash. The count goes on. It has to go on.
Do not mourn in the street. The Holy Lord lives on, and the paladins are listening.
Sixty-two of them, if you believe the Nation. Someone keeps count.
Every Holy Lord is the same Holy Lord, they say. Convenient. Nobody ever has to be replaced.
The Okranites number their kings like cattle. Sixty-two, last I heard.
One man in a chair, sixty-two names deep.
Sixty-two Phoenixes and not one of them ever asked us.
They number their Holy Lords. We number our dead. Ours is the longer count.
Another Phoenix, another purge. The name changes, and the flame doesn't.
The flame came back sixty-two times. We haven't yet counted our own.
Humans light a fire and keep it for a thousand years. They call that faith. We call it fuel.
The Holy Lord who was before this Holy Lord said the same things. Some of us remember. It wasn't the same man.
Sixty-two of them, the humans say. We say the same fire.
A new Holy Lord, and the same sermon. We've heard it burn before.
The sixty-second watches over us. Walk in the light, outlander.
Praise the Flame. Praise the Lord.
The Flame has no end and neither does the Lord.
Sixty-two and counting. Don't count too loudly.
The Guiding Light teaches that the horned were made human, brothers of the faithful. Then the sin grew in them, and the horns after.
Horned devils were our brothers once. The book says so. The book also says what happens to brothers who fall.
The beasts grew horns when they turned from the light. That is not a rumour. That is the third handbook.
The horned were created human. That is the teaching. What they chose after is the lesson.
The priests say we were made human once. Say it to a horn and see what comes back.
Before Kral we don't speak. Humans make up the rest.
Horns or no horns, I have never met a flatskin who could stand where I stand.
Word is, something made us. I say something broke our teachers and we did the rest.
I've heard a skeleton call a Shek human. The Shek looked insulted. I was oddly pleased.
Humans, Shek. The horns don't change what's under them. We're slow to notice differences.
The horned ones are gentle with us, when they aren't hitting us. I don't understand it.
Created human, the book says. I've never been sure what that means for them.
They say the Shek were people once. Bad business to repeat it to a Shek.
Priests say horns came late. Shek say priests came late. I bet on the horns.
Don't ask a Shek where his people came from. Ask him about the weather.
Ask a Holy Nation priest and a Shek what the horns mean. Run before the second answer.
The horned were brothers once, the book says. Tell that to the paladins.
Once brothers, now beasts. The book is plain.
Horns grow where light was refused. Keep your distance from such.
The horned were made human, then fell. Don't make the same mistake.
They say the Eye went dark long ago. The burning in Venge never did.
Venge is bad in daylight. Walk it at night, if you walk it.
Something up there still works. The old ones swear to it. Something up there also stopped. They swear to that too.
I don't cross Venge. The ground is bare as a skull, and not from the wind.
Whatever watches over Venge is older than the Empire. I'd like to ask it about its warranty.
The ruin at the Eye is quiet now. Quiet is worse. Something stopped, and nobody wrote down what.
Burn marks on the old stone, the long kind, from above. The books don't agree what made them.
Reports of a light over Venge. Reports of an older light that stopped. Nobody can cite either.
Something over the Eye stopped working. I remember the quiet more than the work.
One of them stopped. I think. A memory, or a story I was told.
Don't stand under the light in Venge. I can't tell you how I know.
Some quiet is the end of something. The Eye is that kind of quiet.
Burning lands in the east. A light that cooks from above. A scholar once told me it isn't weather. I haven't slept well since.
There are zones on the map nobody sells guides to. Venge is the first one the guild skips.
The east burns by itself. We call it a tax on travel. The scholars call it unknown.
Nobody mines Venge. The ore is fine. The sky is the problem.
They say nobody walks Venge by daylight, outlander.
They say Venge is not a road.
The Eye is quiet, I heard.
They say Venge by day is a funeral you attend alone.
I remember boats. Many boats. I don't remember water, but I remember the boats.
There were ports where there's only dust. I'm not sure it's a memory.
People loved their boats once. I think I'm fond of them for no reason.
I remember a harbour. I've never seen water that deep.
The old harbours are inland. Work that out and you have the start of a thesis.
Old harbours stand dry and far from the shore. Somebody was on the water here once.
The coast was further in. The scholars measure it and look ill.
The shore moved. We have the maps and the shame.
Old hands say there was a harbour out in the muck once. Boats in a bog.
The swamp had water before it had weeds. Some of us can feel it, some of us are just drunk.
Old Swamper told me the muck was a bay once. He also told me the moon was a bad egg.
Boats in the bog. Somebody believed in them once.
The old folk say the water stood higher. They say a lot. They're usually right about the weather.
I found a hull on a hill once. I didn't stay to ask how it got up there.
Old hulls sit far from any water. The old folk shrug.
Used to be more water, they say. Used to be a lot of things.
The ground ran red in the Rebellion, my grandmother said. The nobles shut their gates while the poor ate dust.
Drought, then famine, then the guild caravans that never came. Rogues on the roads, so I hear.
The nobles took what rations came and locked the doors. I'd have done the same, and I won't forgive myself for saying so.
We don't speak of the Rebellion near an official. We speak of the weather.
Don't look at the nobles. Don't look at their windows. My mother looked once, in the Rebellion.
They locked the gates and let us starve. We haven't forgotten. We haven't said so, either.
The laws got harder after. Nobody tells you which laws.
The red year taught us two things. Don't say what you saw, and don't be hungry near a noble.
The Empire starved its own and called the survivors criminals. We just call them neighbours.
Nobles bidding over grain while the poor ate each other. Good riddance to the rule they made.
Half the swamp came from somewhere the Rebellion burned.
The Empire fed its nobles and fined its poor. Then it was surprised.
My folk had a farm before the red year. Now we have a road and a knife. Fair trade, nobody asked.
They called us rebels. We were hungry. The words don't mean the same thing.
The Rebellion wasn't a war. It was a very large mistake that people had to die of.
Lady Tanaka wrote it down. She was the one who shut the gate.
Heathens killing each other over cats and bread. Okran was not mocked.
The Empire ate itself in the red year. We watched from the hills and said nothing, as scripture teaches.
The Empire fought itself over bread. Okran has no use for such weakness.
Okran watched the Empire starve and wasn't surprised.
Humans starve over coin. Some say our kind raided the aid wagons. Nobody admits it. Nobody asks a Shek twice.
The Empire starved because humans would rather hoard than share. We saw it. We did not stop it.
Rogues blocked the aid wagons, so I hear. Some had horns. We don't discuss it.
The red year was human business. Our business is the sword.
Keep your voice down. The nobles have long memories.
Not a word about the red year, stranger.
The red year isn't a story. It's a grave.
We learned to keep our eyes down. Tell the nobles we did.
Grim feeds what crosses her to her hounds. Hash found that out, and so did his clan.
Big Hash is dead and the Stalkers are gone. Grim runs the swamp now. Say it plainly and live long.
She wrote kind letters to Hash once. Then the letters stopped, and so did he.
Her hounds are fed. Everything else in the swamp is on credit.
We were blamed for Hash's brother. Funny how the one with her hounds ready was the one who gained.
Everyone says the Blackshifters did it. Nobody says who gave the order to hunt us for it.
They hang our name on any death that suits Grim.
They found a body at the casino and pointed at us. A club did it, they said. Grim brought hounds.
Five clans, one seat on top. You don't ask how the top seat was won. You ask how to keep your head.
Hash is dead. The Stalkers are gone. That's all the history the swamp needs.
Big Grim got the big seat. The old boss didn't argue.
Hash was boss once. Grim says he left. We say nothing.
Big Grim runs the swamp. Nobody says how she got the seat. Nobody asks twice.
A woman and her hounds. That's the swamp government. The previous one isn't available for comment.
Hash is dead, Grim is alive. The smugglers all know it. The rest of us can guess.
Nobody mentions the Stalkers any more. You can learn a lot from what isn't said.
Don't ask about Hash. Nobody here knows anything.
You new? Then here's the first rule. We don't discuss the old boss.
We're all friends here. Don't ask about Hash.
The big seat is taken. Ask nothing.
Some of us reset when it gets too heavy. We lose the skills too. It's a hard trade, and some call it a fair one.
I do not remember before the city. I have decided that is mercy.
Memory is a thing you carry until it breaks. Then you stop carrying it. Don't look at me like that.
I could recall more. I choose not to.
The skeletons forget everything, I heard. Age, scholars say. A weapon from their enemy, other scholars say.
Ask a skeleton about the old world and he goes quiet. Not the polite quiet either.
They wiped something at some point, long long ago. Skeletons won't say what.
Skeletons forget. We remember being told. It isn't the same, and we pretend it is.
The First Extinction was the darkness's doing. The saviour cleansed the world and the faithful alone endured.
Darkness caused the First Extinction. The Second is coming. That isn't a threat, it's the scripture.
The light was betrayed once. It won't be betrayed twice. That's why we stand watch.
The First Extinction came from darkness. The Second will come from the same, and we'll be ready.
The First Extinction? Plague, my colleague says. A weapon, says the colleague down the hall. We share a roof and not a conclusion.
Whatever ended the old world left no witnesses and a great many theories. Theories are cheap. Digging is dear.
One thing every scholar agrees on. It was quick.
Plague, weapon, flood. A scholar for each. Not one of them has been to the right ruin.
Humans cry about cities that drowned. Warriors do not dwell on what is gone.
The old world ended. So will this one. A warrior meets it standing.
The old world fell. Warriors stood. That is the whole story.
Cities drowned. Our people were not there to see. Good.
Big Hunger come. /CANNIBALHA/ Ate all. Some still eating.
Old world have big hunger. Dhey eat dhemselves. /CANNIBALHA/. We learned from dhem.
Big Hunger take many. We take dhe rest. /CANNIBALHA/
Old world full. Dhen empty. Now we fill it. /CANNIBALHA/
Every old family in the Cities has a grandfather who walked here from somewhere worse. Don't ask which somewhere.
We left when leaving was still possible. That's the only founding story I trust.
The Cities weren't planned. They were what was left standing when people stopped believing in the old throne.
My family doesn't say where it came from. It says it arrived, and that's enough pride for one table.
We were here before the lamps went out, stranger.
Our grandfathers left something behind. We would rather not say what.
We weren't always here. Walk gently, stranger.
Old families don't tell where they came from.
Narko lies beneath the roots, hidden from the light, tempting the weak. That's why the faithful don't trust the old trees.
The darkness was thrown into the abyss under the roots of the trees. Don't forget it when you walk at night.
Okran cast his dark half down so it could do no harm. The dark half has been patient ever since.
Every soul must conquer the darkness within, as Okran did. I try each morning.
Okran warms and Narko cools. Ask the Holy Nation which one it burns in.
Heretic is a word the frightened use for the faithful they can't control.
Narko is the half they threw away.
The light and the dark are the same hand, they say. We believe it with some caution.
Plenty pray to both the light and the dark. Only the Holy Nation insists on one and burns people over it.
A god of day, a goddess of night. I pray to both. Just in case.
The Okranites hate the dark and fear the roots. I fear the Okranites, which is more practical.
Many pray to both. Only the Holy Nation insists on one.
People need a shadow to blame. We've been cast as the villain for longer than I can remember.
Agents of darkness, they call us. I'd like to see the contract.
Narko, Narko. There's always a villain, and we always fit the costume.
The shadow, they call us. We never asked to be a story.
Light and dark taste dhe same. /CANNIBALHA/
Dhe holy ones say big dark under dhe trees. We sleep dhere. /CANNIBALHA/ Still ungry.
Dhe holy ones fear dhe roots. We fear dhe holy ones. /CANNIBALHA/
Dark under dhe trees? We dig dhere.
Keep out of the old roots after dusk, outlander. The faithful don't rest there.
The roots remember, outlander. Rest in the open.
Narko tempts from below. Keep your heart in the light.
Do not sleep where roots grow thick. The faithful know why.
Kral died with a hundred swords around him and passed to Gateway. A warrior asks no better.
Only a warrior's death opens Gateway. I don't talk about dying old. It's a wound that doesn't close.
There are fewer of us every year. The ones who go, go well.
A man who lost his horns still carries Kral's name. He carries my pack too. That's the order of things.
My knees know the weather. I don't ask my years. It shames a warrior to be counted that high.
I should have gone at Kral's side. I'm still here. That's the hard part.
Dying in bed is for flatskins. I'm too slow for the other way.
I counted my years once. I won't do it again.
A pagan cult of beasts. Their glory is throwing themselves away. The Flame can help them find it.
They worship a corpse called Kral and call the afterlife Gateway. Gateway will have no room for them.
Their Gateway has no gate. It has a pyre. The Flame is happy to provide.
Cult of beasts. A Shek who dies well meets us at the Flame.
A warrior cult that keeps throwing itself away. Good for business. There are always fewer of them.
Shek talk of dying well as other men talk of dinner. Don't join the conversation.
Honour is a fine sentiment for a customer who pays up front. The Shek do neither.
A people that keeps dying on purpose.
Dying for a name is an old habit of the living. We say nothing, and we listen.
Dying for a name is an old habit of the living.
Honour, glory, Gateway. The living need such words. We let them have them.
I've watched many march to a good death. I've never learned to clap.
A warrior dies well, they say.
Honour before death, outlander. Learn it or leave.
Gateway waits. We are in no hurry. Neither are you, by the look of your boots.
Gateway is not a place for the lazy.
If you die well, I'll find you there.
We know no-hive that walked out of the hum. This one doesn't look at them long.
The quiet after the hum is the worst. No-hive say they hear nothing.
When the hum is gone, a hiver stops. Some of us walk. Some of us don't know why we walk.
We were taught not to speak of the ones who lost the hum. We speak of them anyway, softly.
Met a hiver once, alone, no hive. He kept pausing mid-sentence, like listening to a door.
The ones who lost the hum, bug men call them. They stop talking in the middle of words.
A hiver without a hive is a bad bargain and a sadder story.
One of them stood in a field once, as if waiting for a call.
Hivers get quiet when their kin get lost. Not sad quiet.
Ask a hiver about the queen and the room changes. Nobody has ever seen her. Nobody wants to be the one to say so.
Bug men don't discuss the queen. They discuss weather. It means the same thing.
A hiver goes quiet when he hears the hum is gone. I've seen it.
We hear you. We don't hear the hum around you.
The hum is soft today. Be soft with it.
Quiet here. It's good quiet. Not all of it is.
We listen for the hum. You must listen for us.
Don't look at them. Don't say the word. It's the Vault. That's all I'll say, and too much.
Enemies of the nobility go to the Vault. Nobody describes it. That's the whole description.
A cousin went to the Vault. We don't set a place for him. We don't say his name.
Nobody gets out of Tengu's Vault. A man who says otherwise is selling something.
The Vault takes rebels and keeps them. We take our own risks and keep them too.
You can be hung for less than what they do in the Vault. That's the nicest thing I can say about it.
We don't talk about the Vault.
The nobles built a place for people like us. We built a place for people like them.
Half the people we pull out of chains have heard of the Vault. None of them have seen it.
Tengu's Vault. There's a name that makes a tired man sit up.
We have emptied a lot of cages. The Vault is the one door we haven't found.
Whatever is in the Vault, the people who left it won't say.
Don't breathe near the nobles. They say there's a torture Vault for rebels and anyone else who irritates them.
If you hear screaming near Skimsands, you didn't hear it.
Don't mention the Vault where nobles can hear. Don't mention it where their servants can hear either.
Skimsands is quiet. That's how you know where the Vault is.
Keep moving. Don't look at the high houses.
You didn't hear anything, stranger.
Don't stare at the high gates.
The Vault is a rumour. Keep it that way.
The painted ones are descendants of the northern labs. Toxins, experiments, famine, take your pick.
Devolved from the ancient scholars, I say. The labs poisoned them and they forgot how to cook properly.
The cannibals are the best argument for a funded research station. Or a very large wall.
Of all the theories, I like the one with the poison best.
Some of my colleagues say the cannibals are older than the labs. Invaders. They ate the ancients. I find that comforting, in a bleak way.
The labs in the north have blood on every wall. Whose, we don't agree.
Invaders or heirs. The bones in the labs aren't decorated with the answer.
The cannibals have the labs now. Whoever had them first isn't in a position to object.
Machinists say cannibals are devolved scholars. Tech hunters say they're tribes that outlived the Ancients. Everyone agrees to avoid the plains.
I don't care where they came from. I care where they're going, and that's toward my dinner.
Descendants, invaders, devolved, born that way. They all eat the same.
Either the cannibals were clever once or the clever ones were food. Both are comforting in their way.
Whether they fell from clever people or outlasted them, they die the same under an arrow.
We have two enemies up here, the ones who burn you and the ones who eat you.
Some say they're the old clever ones gone wrong. Their arrows don't seem clever.
I don't care if they were scholars.
They do not eat us. They hate us anyway. I have a theory about that and I keep it to myself.
The cannibals hate us. We're the only ones who don't taste of anything.
Some of them look at us as if we remind them of something. We prefer to look away.
They fear us for something we don't remember. That's fair. We fear ourselves for the same reason.
Cannibals scream a name when they see us. It isn't ours. It might have been once.
Dhe glass place in dhe north. Some say we came from it. Some say we came to it.
Dhe old ones dhat were in dhe shiny place are quiet now.
Dhe shiny place is ours now. /CANNIBALHA/ Dhe ones before are not complaining.
Our elders say we were dhere first. Dhe odher elders say dhe opposite. Dhey argue with full mouths.
High Priest Varloo says the Hub can't be held while Narko's darkness covers it. He wants the first of her minions destroyed.
Every time we take the Hub we lose it within months. Varloo says Narko. I say walls take more than prayers.
Varloo says the first dark ones must fall before Narko's grip loosens. I say a wall must stand first.
Varloo wants the dark ones destroyed first. The Hub is an afterthought to him.
Narko shook the southern wall down, Varloo says. I saw the rubble.
High Priest Tyluig says it is not Narko. He says Okran's light wavers because we let our own house rot. Women forward, children shaming fathers.
Varloo blames the dark. Tyluig blames us. The priests haven't stopped arguing and the Hub hasn't stopped falling.
Tyluig says we must purify ourselves. The Hub falls anyway. Perhaps we are not pure enough yet.
Tyluig preaches purification. The Hub preaches silence. The Hub is winning.
Sentinels vanish at the Hub, voices in the walls, empty rooms. Say what you like about the reason. I will not stay a night.
They told us to retake the Hub. Nobody told us to stay.
The Hub keeps taking sentinels. We keep sending them. The priests call that faith.
Wraiths took a brother from us at the Hub. Nobody found a body. We were told to be calm.
The Hub is cursed, the report said. The report was approved.
We sacked the Hub and left it burning. Ask why we left. We do not answer.
The Hub holds nothing worth a warrior's death. We took what we wanted, and the place took something from us.
The Hub is a burnt place now. Ask no more.
We left the Hub and didn't look back. A warrior doesn't look back.
The Hub changes hands like a bad coin. Empire, Nation, Shek, and now the ruin belongs to whoever sleeps there.
The Hub was a good town. Then three banners learned it was good.
The Hub fell to the Empire, then to the Nation, then to nobody. Even the dust moved on.
Hub is a bad address. Rent is free and nobody collects.
Don't ask about the Hub. The priests disagree and the walls fall regardless.
The Hub is a bad place to be stubborn. The priests argue, the walls fall.
Lost the Hub again, did we? The priests have a reason every time.
Another priest, another reason. The Hub keeps falling.
The Hub is a place for the stubborn and the damned.
Okran and Narko are two hands of one hand. The Nation only wants to hold one.
Some of us pray to the light. Some to the dark. Most to both, just to be safe.
The light needs the dark to mean anything. Say that in Okran's Pride and see what happens.
We pray out loud here. That's the first thing we took from them.
Okran warms, Narko cools. Neither one asked for a throne.
The old women say the great father split in two so the world could breathe. I like that better than the sermon.
The Nation burns doubt. We feed it.
A god can have two halves. A village needs more than one.
I prayed to the light for the first thirty years. The dark answered, so I switched.
Heretic. They called me that for asking a question. I'd like the question answered.
Okran left the Nation. Or the Nation left Okran. We took his half of the sky and kept it.
I met a priest who asked me which half of god I preferred. I said the one that stops the fire.
Both halves bless your road, friend.
Walk in the light. Rest in the dark. Both are kind to those who earn them.
You've done well by us. The two of them will remember.
Light keep you, dark keep your secrets.
Doubt is allowed here. So are guesses. Welcome.
You're welcome in Flotsam. Doubt is allowed here.
Eat first. Pray after. We don't mind the order.
The Nation wouldn't let you sit.
You can sit. Nobody here will ask what you were. Everybody will ask what you'll do.
Half of us wore the iron. The other half is still angry about it.
A smell stays longer than a bruise.
Hands where I can see them, friend. Old habit. I've been on the wrong end of hands.
I touch my neck when I think. Everybody says so. Nobody in this room has a better habit.
Freedom is a debt. Most of us are paying it forward and some of us are paying it back.
They laughed when we said we would burn the slave market down. Now they lock the doors.
Funny how the iron stays heavy after it comes off.
Good to see a friend with their head up.
One more who walks free. Keep walking.
Every chain you break makes the next one easier.
You walk free because someone else did first.
You wore the iron. So did a lot of us.
Freed, eh? Eat something. We'll talk after.
No questions. Just a seat and a bowl.
The iron comes off. The habit stays. We'll help with both.
Sit. We'll get you something hot.
Those irons won't stay on you long, friend.
I know that weight. We will get them off.
Hold still. We have a key somewhere, and we have patience everywhere else.
Don't let them see you flinch.
I'd love to explain. I'd also love to finish this chapter. One of us will lose.
The books say what they say. The ruins say what they say. The gap is my career.
Ancient isn't a word. Ancient what? When? Be specific, I charge by the adjective.
Someone else digs. I read what they bring. It's a very civilised arrangement.
Three weeks to reach the ruin. Nothing in it. The lady will wring my neck.
Anything buried can be sold. Everything else is weather.
Nobody comes back from the Ashlands. That is why the rumours are so good.
Spiders, mostly. They don't pay a wage.
Don't touch anything old. Don't touch anything that looks old. When in doubt, ask me.
Careful. That mud is a primary source.
Please don't lick the artefacts.
Don't breathe on the manuscripts.
Anything worth a cat? Everything is worth a cat to the right fool.
Found something? Show me. I'll lie about the price.
If it was buried, it was valuable. If it was buried deep, it was cursed.
Relics, stranger? I buy, I sell, I complain.
Bring me what you find. I'll say it's worthless, and then pay you.
You, again. Good. I need someone else to take the risk.
Bring me the heavy things. I'll pay in gratitude. Possibly cats.
Dangerous? Yes. Profitable? Probably. I'll watch from here.
The Empire took my farm. You have food. You see where this goes.
I don't hate you. I'm hungry. It makes me worse than hatred.
Uncle Simion has a mouth full of dirt and a heart of gold, mostly.
We hit the roads, not the poor. That's the rule, even when the poor hit back.
Got any food? I'll pay in good wishes.
We're the ones the nobles forgot, and we remember.
Don't mind the knives. They're for the Empire, mostly.
My farm is gone. My boots are not. Pass.
Farmers with swords. That's all the Empire made us. Credit where it's due.
We planted wheat once. Now we plant ambushes.
Everybody in the Empire has a landlord. We just stopped paying ours.
My hands remember wheat. My knives remember the Empire.
They told us to farm or starve. We chose a third thing.
Friend of ours. Sit, eat. The soup is mostly broth.
You are the first who did not look away. Thanks.
Uncle will want to hear about this. He pretends he doesn't.
The nobles forgot us. You didn't.
Sit. Eat. I'll pretend the soup is better than it is.
A friend in need is an opportunity, and I'm a very good friend.
No rush on the debt. I just like knowing where you sleep.
Everyone owes someone. The trick is who holds the paper.
You look like you need cats. I look like I have some.
I never raise my voice. People hear me anyway.
Interest is a gentle word. I like gentle words.
I remember exactly what you owe.
A loan is a leash made of kindness.
Pay me in cats, or in favours. I prefer favours.
I don't break legs. I know people who do, and we're on good terms.
Debt is a family. You're always welcome to join.
I lend to anyone who can scare me. So far that's nobody.
Nobody here tells me what to do. Well, Grim does. But she is pretty about it.
Sit, drink. You look like you spent a fortune on fear.
No taxes, no chains, no sermons. Enjoy it before the knife arrives.
The nobles can keep their silk. I have a good stick and a better pipe.
I laughed at a priest once. He's still running. Best day of my life.
Free air smells like smoke and bad decisions.
Come back tomorrow and I'll deny this conversation. Also, buy me a drink.
Someone once offered me a title. I used it to light my pipe.
The hemp grows here. The sermons don't. That's the whole argument.
Hoy, traveller. Got a smoke? A drink? A reason to stay alive?
Nobody here asks what you are. Skeleton, Shek, whatever.
Relax. Nobody here's plotting. Not today.
Drink? Smoke? A song? I'll take any of the three.
Nobody here's in a hurry. Except you, apparently.
Friend of the swamp. Have a drink on me. Don't tell Grim.
You are good people. For a wanderer.
Anything you need, friend. Except the good drink.
The swamp likes you. I wouldn't push your luck, but it likes you.
The beast-hunter in the fancy chair. Sixty-two of them, one chair.
Their Holy Lord is a man in a bright hat who burns people. We have no use for him.
A king the Nation keeps raising from the dead. We would have buried him twice.
Sixty-two lords in a row, and they haven't learned to hold a sword. That's the Nation.
Big wise dhing in dhe old days. Maybe edible. /CANNIBALHA/
Dhe tin ones say a big one gave all. Dhe big one was dhe best meat, maybe.
Tin ones say big one gave himself. We say we would have taken a bite. /CANNIBALHA/
Stobe? Dhey say dhe name and go quiet. Good meat for dhe shy. /CANNIBALHA/
People say Narko lies in the roots. I say the Nation keeps its own graves well tended and the rest of the garden poorly.
Roots and abyss and temptation. A very large sermon for a very small garden.
The great father split in two. The Nation kept one half and put the other under a tree.
Under the roots, people say. I say the Nation buries what it fears, and that's all I need to know.
Holy Lord lives long. Many Holy Lords. Dhey all taste dhe same? /CANNIBALHA/
Fire men say dhey are reborn. We say dhey are reheated.
Phoenix burn good. Many Phoenix burn. Dhe smell is always same. /CANNIBALHA/
Dhe big lord die and come back? Dhen we eat him twice. /CANNIBALHA/
Horned beasts were brothers once. Even brothers can burn.
The book tells us what the horned are. The book doesn't say they can be saved.
Brothers once, and now vermin. The Flame will teach the lesson again.
We hold no hatred, only duty. The horned must be taught.
Horns were not in the plan.
Some days I can't remember where I was going.
I reset once. I would not recommend it. I would not recommend not doing it either.
Ask nothing about before. I'd only invent it.
My memory is shorter than my body. That's my own fault.
I heard the Rebellion was a drought and a locked gate. They say the poor did it. They say the poor were right.
Don't talk about the old Emperor near an official. Don't talk about the new one either.
Red ground. That is what the Rebellion left. It is still there if you dig.
Drought, then nobles, then blood. In that order, every time.
A hundred swords closed on Kral and he still stood.
I fight to reach the other side. Do not call it a sickness. Call it a destination.
The ones who die well are waiting. I do not want to keep them long.
We don't hurry to Gateway.
The Emperor keeps what he must keep. A Vault is a reasonable thing for a reasonable state.
I don't know what's in the Vault. I know who isn't in it, and I'd like to stay on that side.
A Vault is a reasonable place. The Emperor is a reasonable man. That's what we say.
Order has costs. I don't ask who pays.
The Nation holds the Hub for a while and loses it. We've been here since before the last priest. Walls aren't our problem.
Varloo, Tyluig, whoever. They argue about why the Hub can't be held. We just hold it, and pour drinks.
The priests blame Narko, or blame themselves.
Priest blames the dark, priest blames the sinners. We pour.
Hive limbs came before the skeleton ones, people say. Odd for a people who don't talk about the past.
Economy arms are a hive trade. A hiver won't tell you the rest.
Skeleton limbs, hive limbs. Trade secrets travel with the supplier.
The bug men made the first limbs, people say. Their eyes tell you to stop asking.
There was a time hive and skeleton shared something. We don't say what.
A skeleton limb in a no-hive shop makes us uneasy. It should not. It does.
Hive and skeleton once shared a bench. Neither of us remembers who left.
We do not discuss the skeleton limbs in our shops. We repair them.
Okran left the Nation, and the dark shelters us.
They preach one god to burn us. We keep two to keep each other.
I've seen you before. Light, dark, whichever.
Both halves of the god know you now.
We don't stand under old roots at night. Habit from the Nation.
Do you pray, outlander? Either half will do.
Roots are fine in daylight. Don't argue with the Nation about it.
Either half will hear you. Pick the one that's quiet.
The Nation fears the trees. We fear the Nation. A tree has never burned anyone.
Some smells stay. Rust, sweat, fear. I sit at the edge of the room so I can leave.
I have forgotten the faces. I haven't forgotten the sound of the key.
The key made the worst sound in the world. I still flinch at doors.
I don't sit with my back to the room. Ask a former slave why.
Some things come off with the iron.
Rumour has it the sea once stood higher. Rumour has it that I'm paid enough.
If you find an old book, bring it here. If you find an old man, leave him there.
The lab at the northern end of the plains is the best-preserved crime scene in the world.
I asked a skeleton once if it remembered the old sea. It said it remembered boats, which is worse.
